title: POC weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
summary: Weekly pilot sync for Redwood Private (VPC) POC. Reviewed networking progress (VPC peering, route tables, firewall rules), discussed a CUDA driver mismatch on the on-prem GPU hosts preventing the latest runtime upgrade, validated model latency targets after batch tuning and KV cache warm-up, and agreed on next steps: share security docs, schedule rolling upgrade window, run targeted perf benchmarks, and open a support ticket for driver/driver-lib mismatch.
topics: Networking and routing (peering, NAT, route tables)
Runtime upgrade and CUDA driver issue
Performance tuning: batching, kv cache, quantization
Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
action_items: Alex Chen - share Redwood Private security & SOC2 docs and network checklist by 2026-06-19
Priya Patel - open support ticket with runtime team for CUDA driver mismatch (ticket #RDW-4127) and provide ETA by 2026-06-18
Samir Ahmed - confirm maintenance window for rolling upgrade (target week of 2026-06-29) and send available windows by 2026-06-19
Elena Torres - provide VPC route table/export and firewall rules screenshot by 2026-06-18
Marcus Li - run provided perf harness (small workload) and upload logs to shared drive by 2026-06-20
next_steps: Send security pack and network checklist
Run focused perf benchmarks after driver fix
Follow up demo of canary rollout behavior and fallback policies
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start: 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Samir Ahmed (NovaScale CTO), Elena Torres (NovaScale DevOps), Marcus Li (NovaScale SRE), Priya Rao (NovaScale Security)

Summary: quick recap and then deep dive into network and upgrade blockers, some perf numbers shared live.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. Quick roll call — we have Samir, Elena, Marcus and Priya from NovaScale, and from our side Priya, Jamal and myself. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Samir Ahmed: Good, thanks. Busy week but ready to go.
[00:15] Elena Torres: Yep, all good. We pushed a few route updates yesterday — I'll explain.
[00:20] Priya Patel: Great, I'll start with the small agenda: networking status, runtime upgrade blockers, perf tuning updates, security questions, then action items. Sound ok?
[00:28] Samir Ahmed: Yup.
[00:30] Priya Patel: Ok — networking. Elena? status on the VPC peering / routes?
[00:34] Elena Torres: So we finished the VPC peering with the Redwood control plane in our staging account, route tables mostly in place, but we hit an issue where some subnets don't have the NAT gateway route so egress to the internet for the orchestration components is blocked. We also have a couple of NACL rules that are conservative — they were auto-generated by security.
[00:50] Alex Chen: Ok that explains why the agent couldn't fetch the remote module during install, right? That would stop the runtime upgrade.
[00:55] Elena Torres: Yeah exactly. Also the peering is fine but we missed a route for the management CIDR on one route table so traffic to the control plane IPs from our SRE subnet is dropping.
[01:08] Marcus Li: I have a screenshot of the route table, I'll drop it in the shared drive after.
[01:12] Priya Rao: From security side — the NACLs were reduced because of compliance, but we can open temporary exceptions for the upgrade window if needed. We'll need audit logs enabled and KMS integration validated before production.
[01:24] Priya Patel: Perfect. Next — runtime upgrade. We tried to apply the latest Redwood runtime yesterday and hit a driver mismatch on the GPU nodes. The runtime requires CUDA 12.x and the host has 11.7, plus the driver-lib versions are slightly off. The container fails with symbol errors.
[01:42] Samir Ahmed: Right, the on-prem hosts are on older images; we've deferred OS updates for stability.
[01:47] Priya Patel: Understood. We recommended either rolling node upgrades or using the fallback runtime (we have a compat build for 11.7) but the compat build doesn't have the latest perf kernels so latency is higher.
[02:00] Alex Chen: Do you have a preference — do you want us to push the compat runtime so the POC continues, or schedule a rolling node upgrade to the newer driver?
[02:08] Elena Torres: Short term, compat runtime would be easier — avoids a disruptive host upgrade. Long term we plan to schedule host upgrades but need a maintenance window.
[02:17] Marcus Li: Agree. Preliminary perf numbers with compat runtime showed ~12% higher p99 latency on the smallest model and about 8% higher on larger models. Not catastrophically bad but outside our SLO of 300ms p95.
[02:32] Priya Patel: Ok that's helpful. We can run some batch tuning and KV cache warm-up to bring that down. Did you run the perf harness we shared?
[02:40] Marcus Li: We ran the harness but only for a short duration — the KV cache was cold so we saw a lot of startup variance.
[02:47] Priya Patel: That's expected. If you run a 30-minute steady workload the prefix/KV cache should warm and latency drop. Also we can reduce batch size to meet p95 if needed.
[02:58] Samir Ahmed: Can you remind us of the configuration you recommended? Batch size and kv settings?
[03:02] Priya Patel: Sure — for your workload (short prompts, median length ~60 tokens) we recommended batch_size 8, max_latency_target 150ms per token, and prefix cache TTL at 6 hours for the POC. Quantization profile S4 with the compat runtime will keep quality stable. I'll paste the config in the shared doc.
[03:20] Alex Chen: Also note that we can enable intelligent batching that reduces idle latency; it's opt-in during POC.
[03:26] Elena Torres: Good — we'll try that.
[03:28] Jamal Ortiz: On the ops side, we noticed a couple of error patterns during the rolling test — intermittent socket resets between the control plane and the agents when the route flaps. That pointed back to the missing route earlier.
[03:40] Marcus Li: Yes we saw connection resets around 10:15 yesterday during the test.
[03:44] Priya Patel: All of that lines up. Once routes and NAT are fixed, we'll see fewer timeouts and the runtime upgrade can proceed.
[03:52] Priya Rao: Quick security question — you mentioned audit logs and KMS earlier. Do you offer HSM integration or customer-managed keys for Redwood Private?
[03:59] Alex Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; customers can bring their own KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM) for at-rest encryption, and we can configure envelope encryption for keys. We'll include the architecture notes in the security pack.
[04:15] Priya Rao: Also SOC2 — do you have an attestation we can share?
[04:18] Jamal Ortiz: We do; I'll attach SOC2 Type II and our security questionnaire answers in the follow-up.
[04:24] Samir Ahmed: Great.
[04:26] Priya Patel: Perf tuning follow-up — after your node-level driver fix or compat runtime decision, run the 30-minute harness with batching and send us the logs. We'll analyze tail latency and advise batch config changes.
[04:38] Marcus Li: Will do. One more question — routing policy for multi-region fallback: can we route to Redwood hosted replicas if private capacity is constrained?
[04:46] Alex Chen: Yes, we support smart routing policies. During POC we can enable a canary fallback to our hosted endpoint (with data egress controls) but that requires agreement on data classification. For regulated data you can have strict no-egress and we'll respect that.
[05:02] Elena Torres: For now we want no egress — will consider fallback in later phases.
[05:06] Priya Patel: Noted. Also we wanted to mention telemetry: we can produce per-route token cost and latency breakdowns in Console — do you have access to the console in staging?
[05:16] Samir Ahmed: We have read access for the AE account but not full project metrics.
[05:21] Alex Chen: We'll invite you to a staging dashboard with token-level breakdowns. Jamal will handle invites.
[05:27] Jamal Ortiz: I'll send invites after the call.
[05:30] Priya Patel: Ok, next — quick demo of a config tweak I made live: lowered batch to 6 and enabled prefix cache warm-up. You might see a small increase in throughput variance but lower tail latency.
[05:42] Alex Chen: I'm sharing a perf graph now — note the p95 drop after cache warm-up.
[05:46] Marcus Li: I see the graph, that's promising. What's the expected cost delta with batch 6 vs 8?
[05:52] Priya Patel: Roughly a 10% cost increase per token with the smaller batch, but p95 improves ~18% in our tests. We can run a cost/latency tradeoff report and share it.
[06:03] Samir Ahmed: Send that — we'll need it for the exec review.
[06:06] Alex Chen: Will do.
[06:08] Priya Rao: Anything else from security? Also, audit logs retention — can we configure retention to 1 year?
[06:14] Jamal Ortiz: Yes, audit logs can be shipped to your tenant's S3 or SIEM and retention is configurable; we'll include retention options in the doc.
[06:22] Elena Torres: Back on the runtime upgrade: if we go with the compat runtime, is there a feature gap we should be aware of?
[06:28] Priya Patel: The compat runtime skips the newest fused attention kernels and some quantization optimizations, so you will see higher latency and slightly higher memory usage. For the POC it's acceptable but for production we recommend aligning host drivers.
[06:41] Marcus Li: Ok. Also we noticed the model quantization profile caused a minor quality change on one of our prompts — about 1.5% delta in semantic similarity. Is that expected?
[06:50] Priya Patel: Small quality regressions are expected with aggressive quantization. We can test S4 vs S3 and run your eval suite; we usually tie quantization recommendations to eval thresholds you define.
[07:02] Samir Ahmed: We have an eval harness — we'll share a small set of prompts for quantization comparison.
[07:06] Priya Patel: Great. Please drop those in the shared drive.
[07:09] Alex Chen: To recap the blockers: 1) VPC route/NAT issue, 2) CUDA driver mismatch on GPU hosts. Short term: apply compat runtime and run perf harness. Long term: rolling host upgrades and align drivers + enable KMS integration and audit logs for production.
[07:27] Samir Ahmed: That matches our notes.
[07:30] Priya Patel: Ok let's capture action items — Jamal, do you want to read?
[07:33] Jamal Ortiz: Sure. 1) Alex will send security pack and SOC2 docs by Friday. 2) Priya will open support ticket RDW-4127 for driver mismatch. 3) Samir to confirm maintenance window week of 6/29. 4) Elena will upload route table screenshots. 5) Marcus will run the 30-min harness and upload logs.
[07:52] Samir Ahmed: Sounds good.
[07:53] Priya Rao: One last compliance question — do you support SAML SSO for console access?
[07:58] Alex Chen: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. We'll include the SSO integration guide in the pack.
[08:05] Elena Torres: Perfect.
[08:07] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and tickets. Next sync same time next week?
[08:12] Samir Ahmed: Works for us.
[08:14] Marcus Li: Thanks all.
[08:15] Priya Patel: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
